items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: CISA's addition of these TrueConf Server vulnerabilities to the KEV catalog highlights active exploitation that security teams must address immediately.
items.summary: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities affecting TrueConf Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog due to evidence of active exploitation. The added flaws are CVE-2026-72529, which involves missing authentication for a critical function, and CVE-2026-72530, a code injection vulnerability. Under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are required to prioritize the rapid remediation of these high-risk vulnerabilities on publicly exposed assets. CISA strongly encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and patch these flaws to mitigate potential compromise.
key_facts: CVE-2026-72529: TrueConf Server Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
CVE-2026-72530: TrueConf Server Code Injection Vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Organizations should immediately identify and patch TrueConf Server instances to mitigate active exploitation risks associated with CVE-2026-72529 and CVE-2026-72530.

items.title: Medical records, SSNs, and bank details exposed in CareCloud data breach
items.one_liner: This massive healthcare breach exposes millions of individuals to identity theft and targeted phishing attacks, emphasizing the need for robust AWS environment security.
items.summary: Healthcare technology giant CareCloud has confirmed a massive data breach that exposed the personal, medical, and financial information of over 3.75 million individuals. An unauthorized third party accessed one of CareCloud's Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments between March 10 and March 16, 2026, causing an eight-hour disruption to one of its electronic health record (EHR) environments. The exfiltrated data includes Social Security numbers, driver's licenses, passport numbers, medical records, health insurance details, and bank account information. The true scale of the breach was recently revealed when the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) updated its breach tracker.
items.bottom_line: The CareCloud breach highlights the severe risk of storing highly sensitive medical and financial data in cloud environments without sufficient access controls.

claims.text: The CareCloud data breach impacted more than 3.75 million people.
claims.support_span: Healthcare technology giant CareCloud has confirmed that a data breach earlier this year impacted more than 3.75 million people, making it one of the largest healthcare data incidents disclosed this year.

items.title: Microsoft Patches Severe Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Allowing Remote Code Execution
items.one_liner: Microsoft patched a CVSS 10.0 deserialization RCE flaw in Entra ID (CVE-2026-69836), confirming no active exploitation.
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed and addressed a maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-69836, CVSS 10.0) in its cloud identity service Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD). The flaw stems from untrusted data deserialization, permitting unauthenticated attackers to execute remote code over the network. Although initial advisories erroneously stated active in-the-wild exploitation, Microsoft clarified that the issue was identified internally by Robert Fitzpatrick and was patched without requiring customer action. The service mitigation has been deployed across cloud infrastructure.

items.title: MalSkills: Detecting Malicious Skills in the Agentic Supply Chain via Neuro-symbolic Reasoning
items.one_liner: Essential reading for anyone using third-party "skills" or plugins in their LLM agent workflows.
items.summary: MalSkills is a neuro-symbolic framework designed to detect malicious modules (skills) in the agentic supply chain. It combines symbolic parsing with LLM-assisted semantic analysis to extract security-sensitive operations and construct a skill dependency graph. By reasoning over this graph, it can identify suspicious workflows that traditional static or dynamic analysis might miss. In a real-world scan of over 150,000 skills from public registries, MalSkills flagged 620 potentially malicious items, 400 of which were confirmed as malicious.
items.bottom_line: Automated neuro-symbolic analysis has successfully identified hundreds of malicious packages in public LLM agent registries, proving the reality of agentic supply chain attacks.

items.title: Connecting the Dots: Securing the Overlooked Corners of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Supply Chain
items.one_liner: The ChainDrop npm worm highlights how attackers poison CI/CD pipelines and developer environments to harvest cloud secrets and propagate malware.
items.summary: Recent threat intelligence from Unit 42 highlights a massive shift in supply-chain attacks toward poisoning the software development lifecycle (SDLC) rather than targeting finished applications. A notable example is the ChainDrop npm worm, which infected over 400 packages—including keyv and cacheable-request—using a stealthy three-step chain involving modified preinstall hooks and the Bun runtime. The worm reads live process memory from GitHub Actions runners to harvest temporary OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens and credentials, backdoors developer tools like VS Code, and uses Ethereum blockchain transactions for dynamic command-and-control communication. Because modern applications are assembled from thousands of indirect open-source dependencies, these attacks compromise developer laptops, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud environments before code ever reaches production.
items.bottom_line: The ChainDrop worm infected over 400 npm packages by exploiting preinstall scripts to harvest GitHub Actions tokens and backdoor developer environments.

items.title: Android Car Malware Spreads Through Built-In Updaters for Ad Fraud, Proxy Botnet
items.one_liner: MoYu Group is hijacking Android vehicle head units via built-in system updaters for ad fraud and proxy botnets.
items.summary: Kaspersky uncovered a new malware strain specifically targeting Android-based automotive head units manufactured by DoFun to build residential proxy botnets and run ad fraud. The malware abuses the legitimate 'TWCore' system updater app and its MQTT broker channel to download a dropper called JarService into the local cache. The dropper contacts command-and-control servers to install covert background payloads without a graphical user interface. The campaign has been attributed to the MoYu Group, operators behind the widespread BADBOX botnet infrastructure.
key_facts: Target: DoFun Android vehicle head units
items.bottom_line: Attackers are compromising automotive Android head units via legitimate firmware update channels to establish stealthy proxy botnet nodes.

claims.text: The malware infects Android automotive head units by abusing built-in firmware updaters developed by DoFun.
claims.support_span: "The malware spread through the built-in updaters of Android-based automotive head unit firmware," security researcher Dmitry Kalinin said. "This is the first documented case of malware found on a car head unit with an infection chain specific to that type of device."

claims.text: The activity is attributed to MoYu Group, linked to the BADBOX proxy and ad fraud scheme.
claims.support_span: The activity has been attributed with high confidence to the MoYu Group, which was outed by the HUMAN Satori Threat Intelligence and Research team last year as part of a broader ad fraud and residential proxy scheme dubbed BADBOX.

items.title: Johnson Controls Simplex Incident Manager
items.one_liner: Johnson Controls Simplex Incident Manager (<=V2.01) exposes plaintext credentials in memory (CVE-2026-27875).
items.summary: Johnson Controls has disclosed a vulnerability (CVE-2026-27875) affecting Simplex Incident Manager versions 2.01 and earlier across worldwide critical infrastructure installations. The application stores user passwords and authentication tokens in cleartext within system memory during execution (CWE-316). A local attacker with low privileges can extract these credentials using memory-dumping tools to achieve unauthorized application access. Johnson Controls has released patched version v2.01.01 and recommends restricting local host access and deploying memory monitoring.
key_facts: CVE-2026-27875: CWE-316 Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory

items.title: Zombie Card Attack Can Revive Expired Visa Cards for Contactless Payments
items.one_liner: Zombie Card attack bypasses POS expiry checks on expired Visa contactless cards via NFC relay without breaking cryptography.
items.summary: Researchers from UMass Amherst demonstrated 'Zombie Card', a contactless payment attack that revives expired Visa cards for point-of-sale (POS) purchases without breaking cryptographic keys. The technique uses an NFC man-in-the-middle relay to rewrite the unauthenticated Application Expiration Date (TLV tag 5F24) read by POS terminals, while leaving Track 2 data intact. Because Visa Kernel 3's fast Dynamic Data Authentication (fDDA) signature does not cover tag 5F24, offline terminal checks pass if the issuer does not independently verify the expiry date during authorization. Tests across major US banks showed multiple institutions accepted the modified transactions.
key_facts: Protocol flaw: Visa Kernel 3 fDDA excludes Tag 5F24 (Application Expiration Date)
Disclosure timeline: Disclosed May & Dec 2025; presented at 35th USENIX Security Symposium
items.bottom_line: Visa contactless Kernel 3 fails to cryptographically bind the application expiration tag, allowing NFC relays to revive expired cards if issuers omit backend validation.

claims.text: The Zombie Card attack modifies the POS expiration date over NFC without breaking card cryptography.
claims.support_span: Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst have demonstrated an attack that revives expired Visa contactless credit cards for real in-store purchases by rewriting the expiration date a point-of-sale (POS) terminal reads over near-field communication (NFC), without breaking any of the card's cryptography.

claims.text: Visa's Kernel 3 fDDA signature does not cryptographically protect tag 5F24, allowing relay modification.
claims.support_span: According to the paper, Visa's Kernel 3 does not require the two to be consistently bound, and the fast Dynamic Data Authentication (fDDA) signature the terminal verifies excludes 5F24 entirely.

items.title: Critical Elementor Pro bug exposes WordPress sites to RCE attacks
items.one_liner: This critical flaw in a widely used WordPress plugin highlights the risk of multi-loop file validation discrepancies leading to unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in the Elementor Pro WordPress plugin, tracked as CVE-2026-32475, could allow unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary PHP files and execute code. The flaw stems from a validation discrepancy in the File Upload module, where separate loops handle empty filename uploads differently, allowing a crafted multi-part upload to bypass extension checks. Exploitation requires the target site to have a published Elementor form with a File Upload field and multiple file uploads enabled. A patch has been released in version 4.2.2, and administrators are advised to update immediately and inspect their upload directories for rogue PHP files.
key_facts: Affected versions: Elementor Pro prior to 4.2.2
items.bottom_line: WordPress administrators using Elementor Pro must update to version 4.2.2 immediately and inspect their upload directories, as updating does not remove previously uploaded malicious files.
